content:
I found the solution!

It was due to a filter rule that had an additional matching rule underneath the main one. (And no, I have no idea how it got there—I don't remember doing anything with my filter rule list in ages). This additional matching rule (as you can see from the picture) had a blank filter condition where an email address or domain name would normally be entered, which meant that ANY email coming from ANYONE would be sent to my Spam folder.

Deleting that additional matching rule fixed the problem.

When I reviewed my filter rules, the list displayed did not show the additional matching rule for this entry. I have 80 filter rules and this particular rule was number 78 on the list. I started my quest by disabling all of the rules and then sending myself an email from my secondary email address. That email went to my Inbox. OK, so now I knew it was a filter problem—but which one? I then re-enabled the first 20 filter rules and sent a second TEST email. That one also went to my Inbox. I kept doing that until the TEST message went to my Spam folder instead of my Inbox. I then re-enabled that batch of rules one by one until I had narrowed it down to the one I wound up editing.

content:
re :we are not getting the emails to our iPhones until we get out of Thunderbird.

Thunderbird program on your computer has no control over the iphone connectivity to a server.

What type of mail account have you set up in the desktop/laptop Thunderbird? Is it IMAP or POP ?

What type of mail account is set up on the iphone? Is it IMAP or POP ?

What server are you connecting to ? such as gmail, comcast, bt, yahoo etc ?

Possible idea worth checking: It could be you have used up too many cached connections when using Thunderbird, but when you exit Thunderbird those cached connections get released and so you can then connect using the iphone. The server controls the total number of allowed cached connections. The server says total number number of cached connections is not just one device it's all of them together. You can lower the number of cached connections used in Thunderbird to see if auto shutting some helps, but usually the problem is the other way around, Thunderbird gets the problem of access due to too many cached connections and the fault is often the iphone using them. In those cases switching off the iphone helps to close some connections. Is your wife also accessing the same account as that would increase the cached connections used?

cached connections are the number of connections concurrently accessing the server mail account. Imap accounts may have several folders synchronising, downloading mail etc and each is a separate connection. If you have other computes and devices doing likewise then you are using more connections. So if you have left another computer or laptop or tablet or phone etc running a connection via Outlook or Thunderbird or any email client, then they are all using cached connections.

You could try to restrict cached connections in Thunderbird if you are using IMAP to see if it helps. If using IMAP then check this: In Thunderbird

  • Account Settings > Server Settings for the account
  • Click on 'Advanced' button
  • 'Maximum number of server connections to cache' default is set at 5
  • suggest you try '3'
  • Note do not increase more then 5.
  • Click on 'OK'
